title: Demo Scenarios - Known Good Matrix
body:
Last refresh: 2026-02-18 (R. Sullivan)

Purpose
- Single source of truth for which scenarios are safe to run live in the Standard Demo tenant.
- Each scenario has: tenant prerequisites, scripted/canned inputs, “expected output” acceptance criteria, and a Plan B if something flakes.
- Status definitions:
  - GREEN = safe live (passed last 2 regression runs, no known flaky steps)
  - YELLOW = usable with caution (timing / UI drift / occasional output variance)
  - RED = do not run live (broken or too flaky)

Global assumptions (apply to all scenarios unless overridden)
- Tenant: Standard Demo v1 (production-like, sanitized). No customer data. Use only provided prompts/seed data.
- Region default: us-east-1 (unless EU-only is explicitly requested).
- Console dashboards to have open before starting: Demo Overview, Latency (p95), Cost/Token, Errors/5xx, Throttles/429.
- Output variance policy: we show “expected output” as an acceptance envelope (must-hit facts + format). We do NOT promise word-for-word output unless we’re using canned responses.
- Default generation settings for deterministic-ish behavior: temperature=0.0–0.2, top_p=1.0, max_tokens fixed; set seed when supported.

Table (copy/paste friendly)
Scenario ID | Scenario name | Primary persona(s) | Differentiator(s) proven | What we show live (30–120s) | Script / asset | Tenant prerequisites (pinning + config) | Canned input(s) | Expected output / acceptance criteria | Plan B (live failure) | Regression cadence | Last regression result | Status | Owner | Notes
S1 | Hosted API: Streaming Chat (Hello + latency baseline) | Platform Eng, ML Eng | Time-to-first-token, streaming UX, predictable latency | Run a streaming chat request from CLI + show p95 latency panel moving in Console | redwood-quickstarts/pr-613 (Sales Demo Quickstart) + /scripts/s1_streaming_chat.sh | Model pinned: rw-llama-3.1-70b-instruct@2025-12-10 (fp16) route=demo/hosted/chat-stream; rate limit demo-safe | Prompt: “You are Redwood Assistant. In 3 bullets, explain what continuous batching is.” | Must stream within 500ms TTFT (typical). Content: 3 bullets mentioning (1) queueing many requests, (2) dynamic batching, (3) improves throughput. | If streaming disconnects: rerun with non-streaming endpoint demo/hosted/chat (same prompt) and narrate streaming as optional transport; switch to screenshot in deck if Console panel lags | Weekly + pre-demo spot check | 2026-02-14 PASS (TTFT 280ms, p95 1.9s, no 5xx) | GREEN | Colin O'Donnell | Keep it under 60s. If prospect asks “how is this faster?” pivot to batching/caching scenario S5.
S2 | Structured Output (JSON schema) | ML Eng, App Eng | Reliability + parseable outputs; reduces app-side glue | Show request with json_schema; response is strict JSON; highlight validation in SDK | redwood-examples/pr-842 (structured output) | Model pinned: rw-qwen2.5-72b-instruct@2026-01-05 (fp16); response_format=strict_json; gateway validation ON | Prompt: “Extract: company, priority, due_date from this email…” (provided sample email text) | Must produce valid JSON (no trailing text). Keys exactly: company, priority, due_date. priority ∈ {low, medium, high}. due_date ISO-8601 or null. | If model returns invalid JSON: flip to canned response toggle in script (local fixture) and narrate “this is why we enforce schema + retries”; then show Error Analysis panel quickly | Weekly | 2026-02-14 PASS (schema valid 10/10) | GREEN | Simran Kaur | Keep sample email obviously fake (no real names). Do not let prospect type their own email.
S3 | Tool Calling: “Search docs” + grounded answer | Platform Eng, ML Eng | Tool calling + safety via constrained actions; shows developer-first interface | Run chat with tool definition; tool call triggers stubbed search; final answer cites docs snippets | redwood-examples/pr-842 (tool calling) + /fixtures/docs_snippets_v1.json | Model pinned: rw-llama-3.1-70b-instruct@2025-12-10; tool_calling=enabled; tools whitelist includes demo.searchDocs only | Prompt: “How do I set a fallback model on a route? Use docs.” | Must call tool once with query containing “fallback” + “route”. Final answer: 3–5 bullets, references 2 snippet IDs (e.g., DOC-14, DOC-22). Must mention canary/fallback policy at high level. | If tool call doesn’t trigger: re-run with alternate phrasing (saved prompt B). If still no: show pre-recorded output in script (fixture) and pivot to routing/fallback scenario S4 in Console (policy view) | Weekly | 2026-02-07 PASS (tool call hit 9/10; one retry needed) | YELLOW | Renee Sullivan | Slightly flaky depending on model load. Don’t oversell “perfect determinism.”
S4 | Reliability: Routing + Fallback (failure injection) | Platform Eng, SRE-minded buyers | Graceful degradation, policy-based routing, no downtime during model issues | In Console: show route policy (primary + fallback). Trigger a forced 500 on primary in demo; re-run request and show fallback served | /scripts/s4_fallback_inject_failure.sh + Console clickpath screenshot refs | Route pinned: demo/reliability/chat. Primary: rw-llama-3.1-70b@2025-12-10 (region us-east-1). Fallback: rw-llama-3.1-8b@2025-12-10 OR compatible alt. “Failure injection” flag available only in demo tenant (header x-demo-fail-primary=true) | Prompt: “Summarize this paragraph in 2 sentences” (provided lorem) | First run (no injection): model=primary. Second run (injection): response header/model_id indicates fallback. Acceptance: request still succeeds (<3s) and Console shows spike in fallback counter, not 5xx. | If Console UI clickpath changed: use saved view link “Routing Policies (Demo)” and narrate. If failure injection header stops working: switch to “capacity constrained” simulation by toggling route weight (pre-configured) | Pre-demo + weekly | 2026-02-14 PASS (fallback engaged, no errors) | GREEN | Mina Haddad | This is the “hero” enterprise proof point. Always run after S1 or as first scenario for platform/SRE personas.
S5 | Cost controls: batching/caching impact + token cost dashboard | Procurement-adjacent, Platform Eng | Unit economics levers with visibility; shows Optimize story without a science project | Run same prompt set twice (cold vs warm cache) and show cost/token + latency deltas in Console | /scripts/s5_cache_warm_compare.sh + saved dashboard “Cost & Latency - Demo” | Cache enabled for demo/cost/chat; prefix cache ON; batch window = 20ms (demo-safe); Model pinned: rw-mistral-large-2@2026-01-21 (int8) for cost-focused path | Prompt set: 5 near-identical product Q&A prompts (provided) | Acceptance: Run #2 shows improved cost/token (>=10% better) OR reduced p95 latency (>=10% better). Console must show trace/sample request entries for both runs. | If deltas are small (due to low load): switch to “Batching visualization” panel (prebuilt) + narrate under real traffic deltas are larger; optionally increase concurrency from 1→10 using script flag | Weekly | 2026-02-07 PASS (cost/token -18%, p95 -12%) | GREEN | Logan Wright | Do NOT show absolute $ numbers. Only relative deltas + “ranges” language per PMM guidance.
S6 | Observability: Error analysis + traces (why did a request fail?) | SRE, Platform Eng, Security (audit trail angle) | Faster MTTR; confidence in production operations | Open a known failed request (seeded) and walk through trace: input validation → route decision → model error category | Seeded request IDs list in /fixtures/failed_request_ids.txt + Console saved view “Error Triage - Demo” | Seeded synthetic failures (no sensitive payloads). Logging redaction ON. RBAC: demo role = read-only for traces (driver account only). | Use seeded request ID “FAIL-DEMO-003” | Acceptance: Console displays (1) HTTP status, (2) error category, (3) route/model, (4) timestamp, (5) suggestion text. No raw prompt shown (redacted) unless using safe fixture payload. | If seeded failure aged out: switch to live-induced validation error using an intentionally invalid parameter (e.g., max_tokens=-1) and show gateway validation message instead | Monthly (less likely to drift) + pre-demo check that request exists | 2026-01-12 PASS | GREEN | Chloe Martin | Good “closing” scenario to reinforce production readiness. Also good if prospect asks “what about debugging?”

Scenario ordering recommendations (by persona)
- Platform Eng / SRE: S4 → S1 → S6 → S5 (optional) → S2/S3 if app team present
- ML Eng / App Eng: S1 → S2 → S3 → S5 (optional) → S4 if reliability questions arise
- Security-first: Start with security FAQ (separate doc) + then S6 (redaction/audit trail angle) + S4 (isolation/fallback story). Avoid letting them type sensitive text.

Open issues / TODOs
- S3 tool calling flake rate: investigate whether to pin alternate model or add “tool call reinforcement” system prompt (Simran / Colin). Target: GREEN by next revision.
- S5 delta sensitivity: add “synthetic concurrency” mode that is still safe live (Logan / Renee).
- Add EU-only mini-variant (routing to eu-west-1) for EMEA asks; keep as separate scenario (not in v1) pending tenant support (Lukas request).

Change control
- Any change to model pinning, route names, or Console clickpaths must be reflected in: (1) this matrix, (2) talk track speaker notes, (3) reset checklist.
- If a scenario goes RED, update this sheet + post in #sales (Standard Demo v1 thread) with workaround and ETA.
